text:
alex: Heads up — noticed weird behavior when a route policy TTL expires during a busy window; requests get stuck in 'pending fallback' and never hit the regional fallback. Anyone seen this? repro steps below.

maria: Yep saw this in staging last night. Logs show lease revocation not propagated to the edge for ~20s.

jordan: FYI TTL vs lease revocation are different primitives. TTL = local cache expiry; revocation should be pushed. Feels like we treated revocation as a soft-ttl somewhere.

lee: I dug a bit — route-compiler emits "revoked": true but routers ignore it when manifest_stamp_version < 2. Could be a version-skew guard.

sam: Minimal repro I ran: update policy with `"revoked":true` then hammer with 500rps. Edge logs: `compat_check: stale_policy -> keep` repeatedly; requests queue up.

alex: Repro snippet:
```json
{"policy_id":"p-123","version":42,"revoked":true,"rules": [...] }
```
Edge log example: ``[edge-3] compat_check: policy_version=41 actual=42 decision=keep``

maria: Options I see: 1) push revocation via a pubsub channel so routers get it ASAP, 2) short-circuit routers to consult the lease table for immediate truth, 3) rely on shorter TTLs + canary drains. Tradeoffs: push = complexity, short-circuit = read hot-spot, short TTL = possible flapping.

jordan: My preference is push + graceful drain. Revocation should be a two-phase: mark `draining` (stop new slot assignments) then `revoked` after grace window. That avoids killing in-flight requests and still prevents new traffic.

lee: Implementation questions: we need to make the transition atomic from policy-maestro's POV. Also hedged requests complicate this: a hedged request might go to two backends; if one sees drain and the other doesn't, we could get inconsistent behavior. We need a `drain_start` timestamp propagated with requests.

sam: Also add telemetry tags: prev_policy_id, revoked_at, drain_start, and a reason tag (operator-initiated / autoscale / outage). That will help postmortems.

alex: On ordering between fallback and revocation: if revoked route had no available capacity, should we fallback immediately (to meet latency) or respect revocation (to meet correctness)? I think latency SLO should win for external customer requests; correctness (no access to revoked tenant model) might be non-optional for some tenants. We need policy-level flag `enforce_strict_revocation=true|false`.

maria: Agreed. Add `policy.meta.strict_revocation` default=false. Enterprises can opt-in. Document the semantics.

jordan: Action items: (1) add revocation push channel in policy-maestro (pubsub topic + ack model), (2) add `draining` flag + default 5s grace window, (3) router reads `drain_start` and stops new allocations, (4) telemetry event `route.revoked` + fields.

maria: I'll own telemetry + tests (unit + sim).

jordan: I'll own the policy-maestro push API and small server-side implement.

lee: I'll update router to handle `draining` and `revoked` states; staging canary first. Need a migration plan for `manifest_stamp_version` check.

sam: I'll add an integration sim that folds hedging and preemptive fallback to validate no request loss. Will run perf to check read hot-spot on lease table.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: policy-maestro:canary -> staging at 4512345689 by jordan

alex: Thanks all. Let's reconvene Thu @10 for rollout check and canary metrics (error-rate, avg-latency, fallback-rate). :thumbsup:
